ai.description: This lizard grows to 50 cm with a long, slender tail. It is bright green with dark transverse bands and a distinctive white or cream stripe along the flanks. A prominent dorsal crest is present.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Calotes calotes* is uniquely identified by its exceptionally long tail, which is typically three to four times the length of its body, unlike other similar forest lizards.
ai.habitat: *Calotes calotes* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, often found in dense vegetation or coffee plantations at elevations ranging from sea level to 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Common Green Forest Lizard is primarily diurnal, often remaining motionless on tree trunks to ambush passing insects while relying on its cryptic coloration for defense.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Calotes calotes* is oviparous, laying clutches of 2–10 eggs. Breeding typically occurs from May to September, often peaking during the monsoon season in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Calotes calotes* is found in the Western Ghats and southern India, typically inhabiting moist forests and plantations from sea level up to approximately 2,000 meters.
